title: Choose the Git workspace architecture
description: The product target is a fully working GitHub Desktop-style client, not only a read-only repository visualizer. Decide how Git repositories and operations will work in this IWSDK web application before implementation adds branch, index, commit, or remote-write behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Compare browser-local Git/workspace storage, a server-managed Git service, and any materially different viable approach against IWSDK/WebXR support, persistence, security, portability, and deployment.
Recommend one approach and document its data flow, credential boundary, workspace lifecycle, supported platforms, and known limitations.

Update docs/02-system-architecture.md, docs/03-authentication-and-security.md, docs/04-repository-data-and-api.md, docs/19-api-contracts.md, and docs/10-decisions-and-open-questions.md so they agree with the recommendation.
Do not implement Git write operations, request write permissions, install dependencies, or expose credentials in this architecture task.

steps.description: Inspect the current app and product constraints
steps.details: Read the architecture, security, repository, API, platform, and desktop-style roadmap specs. Inspect only the source needed to confirm the existing runtime and backend boundaries.

Use current official technical documentation for any platform or library claims. Compare the approaches against secure auth, local change durability, WebXR/browser limitations, server deployment, and user control.

steps.description: Record the recommendation and update affected contracts
steps.details: Write one decision with rationale and migration path. Keep unresolved product choices explicit. Do not alter implementation code or permissions.

technicalNotes: The first read-only milestone remains useful but is not the final product target.
No architecture decision may imply success for unimplemented Git operations.
Do not read, print, or modify .env values.
